html:
Kuwait is a small country at the head of the Persian Gulf, between Iraq and Saudi Arabia, made up mostly of one city. The map shows it in 1914 and from 1945 onward.

It began as a trading and fishing town. The Al Sabah family became its rulers in the 1750s, and Kuwait lived from shipbuilding, desert caravans and pearl diving. It lay on the edge of the Ottoman province of Basra. In 1899, worried about Ottoman and German plans, Sheikh Mubarak signed an agreement that made Kuwait a British protectorate.

Oil was struck in 1938 and exports began after the Second World War. Kuwait became one of the richest countries in the world per person, with free schools and health care for its citizens and a large foreign workforce. It became independent in 1961 and was a founding member of OPEC.

In August 1990 Saddam Hussein invaded and annexed Kuwait. A US-led coalition drove Iraq out in the Gulf War of 1991, and the retreating army set the oil wells on fire.
sum: Kuwait is a small country at the head of the Persian Gulf, between Iraq and Saudi Arabia, made up mostly of one city. The map shows it in 1914 and from 1945 onward.
